headline: KINROSS Q2: $844M NET EARNINGS, $726.8M FREE CASH FLOW ON $2.24B REVENUE — 492K oz at $4,483/oz; 42% Margin Surge (NYSE/TSX: KGC)
snippet: Kinross Gold reported Q2 2026 revenue of $2,238.1 million (up 29% year-over-year) on production of 492,326 gold equivalent ounces at a realized average price of $4,483 per ounce, generating $726.8 million in attributable free cash flow and $844.2 million in net earnings ($0.71 per share, beating consensus of $0.66 by 8%). Margins rose 42% to $3,131 per oz sold, operating cash flow reached $1,145.9 million for the quarter, and the company returned $275 million to shareholders while reaffirming full-year guidance — adding Kinross to the growing roster of mid-tier producers delivering their best financial quarters in company history at $4,000+ gold.

headline: ENERGY FUELS: $104M HEAVY RARE EARTH PLANT NOW UNDER WAY IN UTAH — Terbium and Dysprosium Production Circuits Targeted 2027 (NYSE: UUUU)
snippet: Energy Fuels Inc. announced July 29 that a commercial-scale heavy rare earth oxide plant is now under construction at its White Mesa Mill in Utah, with a Phase 1 design capacity of 20 tonnes per annum of terbium and 120 tpa of dysprosium oxide — the two most critical inputs for permanent magnets used in EV motors and wind turbines — alongside 140 tpa of samarium, 20 tpa of europium, and 140 tpa of gadolinium. The estimated US$104 million capital cost is expected to be substantially funded through US government grants and loans, with terbium and dysprosium circuits targeted for completion by end-2027, making Energy Fuels the first company in the Western Hemisphere to move commercial-scale heavy rare earth processing out of China and into operating domestic infrastructure.

headline: LUNDIN GOLD FDN EAST RECORD: 236.62 g/t AU — Development Begins; 108 g/t Over 11.75m at FDNS Also Confirmed (TSX: LUG)
snippet: Lundin Gold Inc. (TSX: LUG) released July 27 results from its near-mine exploration programs at the Fruta del Norte gold mine in Ecuador, with hole UGE-E-26-487 returning the highest-grade intercept ever recorded at FDN East: 236.62 g/t Au over 3.95 metres — and a companion FDNS intercept of 108.61 g/t Au over 11.75 metres from the same campaign. Critically, the company announced that underground drift development has commenced toward FDN East, converting a drill discovery into an active underground development target and signalling that one of the world's highest-grade producing gold mines is actively growing its recoverable inventory in a $4,000+ gold environment.

headline: ROCK TECH SIGNS 7-YEAR BINDING OFFTAKE + US$80M PREPAYMENT WITH TRANSAMINE — Georgia Lake Ontario Spodumene (TSX-V: RCK)
snippet: Rock Tech Lithium Inc. (TSX-V: RCK) signed a binding seven-year spodumene concentrate offtake agreement with Transamine SA, a Geneva-based global commodity trading house, covering up to 100,000 dry metric tonnes per year from the Georgia Lake project in Northern Ontario — ramping from 50,000 dmt in the first year starting in 2028. The deal includes a development prepayment facility of up to US$80 million and preserves Rock Tech's right to redirect the concentrate to its planned Red Rock Lithium Converter in Ontario if domestic battery-grade processing comes online, advancing the 'made-in-Canada' critical minerals supply chain Ottawa has been seeking to build outside Chinese refining dependence.

headline: INZINC HITS 15m @ 7.0% ZINC + 17.5 g/t SILVER — 'Strongest-to-Date' B-9 Apex Zone Discovery at Indy (TSXV: IZN)
snippet: InZinc Mining Ltd. (TSXV: IZN) reported July 29 the strongest drill results to date from its spring 2026 diamond drill program at the Indy Sedex project in central British Columbia, with hole INB-26-027 intersecting 15.0 metres grading 7.0% zinc, 3.2% lead, and 17.5 g/t silver from 67.1 metres depth at the B-9 Apex Zone — including a 3.0-metre Silver-Rich sub-interval at 61.8 g/t Ag, 10.7% Zn, and 11.7% Pb. The results confirm stacked high-grade Sedex-style mineralization at shallow depth in a drill-ready target, a style of deposit that historically hosts some of the world's largest base metal and silver systems.

headline: GREENHEART GOLD IGAB MAIDEN DRILL: 7m @ 5.82 g/t AU — 3 Zones Confirmed 30km From Merian Mine in Suriname (TSXV: GHRT)
snippet: Greenheart Gold Inc. (TSXV: GHRT) released July 29 the first drill results from a maiden 17-hole diamond drill program at its Igab Gold Project in Suriname's Para District, with hole IGBD26-007 at the Koela target returning 7.0 metres grading 5.82 g/t gold — alongside additional intercepts of 8.0 metres at 2.16 g/t Au and 4.0 metres at 4.68 g/t Au in the same zone. The project sits 30 kilometres south of Newmont's world-class Merian gold mine along the Maroni mobile belt, and this is the first drilling ever conducted on the Igab land package, with the Koela, Lemon Tree, and Desiberg targets all showing gold mineralization in the opening program.

headline: MONEY METALS: WHY PCE 'IN-LINE' DOESN'T TELL GOLD INVESTORS THE FULL INFLATION STORY
snippet: Money Metals Exchange's Mike Maharrey argues in his July 29 piece — published on the morning of the FOMC rate decision — that the personal consumption expenditures deflator systematically understates real purchasing power erosion because the index substitutes away from goods as they rise in price, smoothing out the lived inflation experience in food, shelter, and energy where consumers have the least flexibility. For precious metals investors, the practical takeaway is that PCE 'beats' and 'in-line' prints can coexist with genuine household wealth destruction — which is precisely the persistent-inflation environment where gold has historically delivered its strongest multi-year returns.

headline: ASX GOLD MINERS SINK AS SPOT RETREATS TO $4,030 IN ASIA — Post-FOMC Relief Fades; Equities Underperforming Metal Again
snippet: Gold miners led losses on the Australian Securities Exchange on July 30 as spot gold retreated to approximately US$4,030 per ounce in late Asian trading — down roughly $50 from its post-FOMC peak — dragging the S&P/ASX 200 down 0.5% with index-heavyweight miners leading the retreat. The equity underperformance relative to the metal price continues a recurring pattern in this correction cycle: when spot gold consolidates, producers and developers absorb disproportionate selling pressure, compressing the producer-to-spot discount to levels that historically close sharply when the next catalyst — September FOMC, GDP data, or a central bank reserve announcement — arrives.

headline: GOLD SWOT: DPM METALS AND DISCOVERY SILVER BOTH +10% LAST WEEK — China Gold Imports Hit 26-Month High; YTD Flows 76% Above Prior Year
snippet: US Global Investors' weekly Gold SWOT column (July 27) highlights that DPM Metals (TSX: DPM) and Discovery Silver (TSX-V: DSV) both posted 10%+ single-week gains driven by DPM's Q2 production beat and Discovery Silver's resource expansion drilling, while silver was the week's best-performing precious metal at +3.73% with silver ETFs absorbing 1.09 million additional troy ounces in the latest session. The most significant fundamental data point: China's gold imports through Hong Kong reached a 26-month high in the latest reporting month, with year-to-date import volumes running 76% above the comparable prior-year period — a demand-side signal that supports the structural bull case regardless of near-term Fed positioning.
